title: Plan ten years with a Weibull curve and a budget per year

expected.says: Run's report for the tiny fleet matches the expected report

blueprint.signature: def risk_removed(t: Transformer, start: int, request: Request) -> float
blueprint.contract: The coefficient of x[i, start], $k: for each year y of the risk window (request.risk_years(), the window's years from FIRST_YEAR, or the plan's years when window is None) with y >= start, the old unit's PoF at its age in year y minus a new unit's PoF at age y - start, times the unit's CoF, divided by (1 + request.rate) to the power y - FIRST_YEAR. Years before start remove nothing.
blueprint.idea: A replacement's value is the failure cost it avoids each year after it, discounted to today, so a later replacement is worth less.

lesson.title: 7.3.4 Risk Reduction From an Intervention, Year by Year

blueprint.signature: def pof_next(age: float, kind: str) -> float
blueprint.contract: The probability that a unit of this kind, working at `age`, fails within the year: 1 - exp((age / eta)^beta - ((age + 1) / eta)^beta), with beta and eta from KINDS[kind]. It reproduces the fleet's pof column.
blueprint.idea: A Weibull curve gives the PoF at any age, so a plan can value a unit in years it has not reached.

lesson.title: 7.3.1 Probability of Failure and Hazard Curves (Weibull)

blueprint.signature: def build(fleet: list[Transformer], request: Request) -> Built
blueprint.contract: Candidates are the units at least request.min_age old. One binary x[tid, year] per candidate and plan year (request.plan_years(), `years` years from FIRST_YEAR), named `x_<tid>_<year>`; a row `once_<tid>` letting each candidate be replaced at most once; a row `budget_<year>` per plan year keeping that year's replacement cost within request.budget; and the summed risk_removed coefficients as the objective to maximize. Built.x is keyed by (tid, year), Built.budget by year.
blueprint.idea: A start-year variable per unit and year, with a row allowing one start, turns when into a choice the solver makes.

lesson.title: 6.4.1 Start-Time Variables x[i,t] and Timing Windows

blueprint.signature: def feasible(fleet: list[Transformer], request: Request, replace: dict[str, int]) -> bool
blueprint.contract: Fixes x[tid, year] to 1 for each listed unit and its year and every other variable to 0, solves, and answers whether the solver found a plan.
blueprint.idea: A pinned plan now names a year for each unit, so the pin is on the pair.

lesson.title: 12.3.1 Unit-Testing One Constraint at a Time

blueprint.signature: def plan(fleet: list[Transformer], request: Request) -> Plan
blueprint.contract: As before, with request.gap as the solver's relative gap tolerance; the Plan maps each replaced unit to the year of its variable that is 1.
blueprint.idea: A gap tolerance lets the solver stop once its plan is provably close to the best.

lesson.title: 14.3.2 A Ten-Year Budget and Weibull Failure Risk

blueprint.signature: def spend_by_year(fleet: list[Transformer], replace: dict[str, int], outage_cost: int = 0) -> dict[int, int]
blueprint.contract: What the replacements cost in each year, $k: for each year that appears in `replace` (transformer id -> year), the summed cost of the units replaced that year, as a dict sorted by year. Years with no replacement are left out. `outage_cost` is a stub for the next lesson, which charges each outage to its year; this step ignores it.
blueprint.idea: A plan is a map from unit to year, so the report groups it by year and adds up costs; the solver's own rows are not read back.
